Laura / Neha — thanks for the ping. I reviewed Brightwell's redlines and the items in scope. High-level:

- SCCs: agree we should reference the 2024 SCCs and include an Annex A that lists subprocessors + country of processing. I prepared a quick compare file (SCCs-AnnexA-compare.tsv) showing our current Annex vs their requested fields; see attachment.

- Roles: the Order Form does appear to conflate controller/processor wording in two clauses (Sections 2.1 and 5.4). Proposed approach: mark Redwood as Processor for the service, add a short clause that allows Brightwell to act as Controller with mutually agreed data inputs, and add explicit mapping table in the Order Form appendix. That keeps liability limited while clarifying responsibilities.

- Retention/export: 30 days for export is reasonable operationally, but we should add a standard exception for extraordinary data volumes that need phased export (with milestone-driven plan). We can propose a 30/90 fallback (30 days for small exports, 90 days max for exceptional volumes) to be pragmatic.

Next steps: I'll draft language for the SCCs reference + Annex header and a short Order Form appendix mapping. Neha — can you provide the privacy-approved clause for subprocessors (notification/cure periods and audit rights)? If you can send your snippet, I'll stitch it into the draft.

Karthik / Laura — draft clauses below and a short role-mapping table. I've also uploaded a plain-text file with the proposed DPA snippets (DPA_Proposed_Clauses.txt). Feel free to reuse.

Proposed subprocessor clause (snippet):
"Customer acknowledges and agrees that Redwood engages subprocessors to provide the services. Redwood shall: (a) maintain an up-to-date Annex listing subprocessors and the countries in which they operate; (b) notify Customer of new subprocessors at least 30 days before engagement; and (c) provide reasonable cooperation in any Customer-initiated audits limited to compliance with this DPA."

Role mapping (for inclusion in Order Form appendix):
- Redwood Inference: Processor (provides inference platform and model serving)
- Brightwell Inc: Controller (determines purposes and means of processing for customer data)
- Data exports / shared models: subject to export procedure; Brightwell may request data export within 30 days of termination; Brower exception: if aggregate export size > 5TB, export plan with milestones up to 90 days.

SCC reference line (suggested):
"Transfers of personal data outside the European Economic Area shall be governed by the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (as amended or replaced). An Annex to this DPA lists applicable subprocessors and transfer mechanisms in force at the time of transfer."

I think these are conservative and should close the majority of their concerns. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with Brightwell to walk through. My availability: 2027-04-09 between 15:00-17:00 BST, or 2027-04-10 morning.
